Exploring the cosmic applications of supergravity provides a platform to investigate the potential outcomes of this theoretical framework, which could serve as the low-energy effective theory of superstrings-a potential quantum gravity candidate.  Developing inflationary models in supergravity, however, poses significant challenges stemming primarily from the constraints on scalar potentials and complicated interactions within the framework, as well as the excess degrees of freedom.  Addressing these issues requires navigating the constraints on desirable inflationary paths, moduli stabilization to achieve a stable de-Sitter phase, and ensuring the scalars remain heavy compared to the Hubble scale to facilitate single-field inflation.  Additionally, supergravity predicts several non-renormalizable interactions, rendering it an effective field theory that remains valid up to a specific cutoff energy scale, and thus necessitates a re-examination of the scalar potentials and field dynamics to achieve self-consistency at the quantum level.  This thesis, therefore, constructs locally supersymmetric effective field theories of inflation, incorporating recent reforms to the $\mathcal{N}=1$ supergravity formulation that alleviate the constraints on scalar potentials and the number of field degrees of freedom.  Utilizing an action-based approach, we obtain consistent equations of motion for the fields within the framework of the D-term model with the gauge group $U(1)$ and address various field configurations to extract viable solutions. advisors experienced notable gains, largely driven by their trades in commodity futures. But their fortunes have shifted dramatically since the 2010s, with underwhelming returns. Although pinpointing the application protocol can be challenging, solely relying on static characteristics like port numbers can be insufficient. As a result, advanced and adaptive approaches have been developed for more precise identification. In this research, the mechanisms of dynamic protocol detection in widely used open-source network monitoring tools are examined, along with the advantages and limitations of current methods. Our study also highlights the importance of relevant data sets, training strategies, and evaluation metrics in shaping a more robust and practical solution to adaptive protocol detection. in integrated circuits. Another potential means of information transport, magnons derived from spin waves in magnetic materials, is difficult to regulate. However, we found that superconducting strips atop thin magnetic films can completely reflect magnons through their magnetic resistance to stray magnetic fields. The significant frequency shifts resulting from this response effectively halt the forward flow of magnons perpendicular to the magnetic field. By positioning two superconducting gates in parallel with the magnetic field, we were able to create a confined magnon system. The added capability to control coherent magnons enables new functionalities in magnonic devices, including reconfigurable logical circuits and stronger connections to other systems of degrees of freedom.

A potential substitute for Bloom filters is the cuckoo filter, which often needs less storage and processes information faster. A different solution, the Bloomier filter, has been proposed as an expansion of the Bloom filter. A modification to this concept has also been explored, particularly by Dietzfelbinger and Pagh. Their variation of the Bloomier filter can serve approximate membership queries efficiently, though no comprehensive testing of it exists yet. A different filter was developed, the xor filter, as an implementation of their idea, offering more effective efficiency and speeds. Notably, the developed xor filter can surpass both Bloom and cuckoo filters in performance, all while consuming even less storage space than these solutions. A compact variant of the xor filter was also designed (xor+), resulting in storage needs similar to or smaller than already compressed sequences while providing similar speeds to those seen in Bloom filters.

Specifically, servers utilize DBSCAN with S2PC to cluster the legitimate data majority without acquiring private user data. Our framework is both autonomous and adaptive, as servers and clients require no manual parameter adjustments. urIPS 2021 - AWS Deepracer challenge, which required developing a self-driving vehicle model that interacts with its environment through action-reward interactions. The competition was part of The AI Driving Olympics (AI-DO), a series that fosters embodied intelligence advancements in autonomous driving, by benchmarking the progress in applied autonomy. We integrate these techniques into the data of five well-known exoplanets, including those similar to Earth and our neighboring hot Jupiters, to improve their respective radial velocity and transit light curve analyses. nervous activity proposed by McCulloch and Pitts in 1943, a new continuous-time model, known as the McCulloch-Pitts network (MPN), has been developed for sequence learning and prediction in neural networks. By leveraging the framework of random fields on function spaces, the model can be analyzed through the lens of statistical physics. Our investigation into MPN reveals that it can learn complex, generative models of time series data, and our results show that the model's ability to make precise predictions is tied to the entropy of its state space. To validate our model's effectiveness, we tested it on several tasks, including learning periodic signals, tracking periodic signals, and predicting chaotic times series data. 2022 Out-Of-Vocabulary (OOV) challenge.
The competition highlighted an underinvestigated area in Optical Character Recognition (OCR) technology: accurately reading previously unseen text in real-world images during model training.
The dataset compiled for the competition comprises a diverse collection of 326,385 images, encompassing 4,864,405 text instances.
To address the challenge, a distinct validation and test set was created, comprising scene text that was not present in the training data.
The competition featured two recognition tasks: a holistic approach to reading full text and a focused task involving cropped text segments.
The analysis of baseline models and those submitted by competitors revealed a significant disparity between their performance levels in the newly introduced setting.
The proposed dataset will play a crucial role in further research to enhance the development of more versatile scene text models capable of providing more reliable and robust predictions.

Neural Networks (CNNs) are emerging due to rising demands for accurate predictions and thorough analyses. However, they necessitate a considerable amount of computational power and time for processing. Previous studies on pruning have focused on enhancing inference efficiency, but there's been limited research on effectively decreasing training costs. Our proposed framework, ClickTrain, efficiently and accurately enables both end-to-end training and model pruning for CNNs, distinguishing itself from previous work with fine-grained architecture preservation through pattern-based pruning, precise weight estimation, and compiler-optimized calculations. As a result, ClickTrain can deploy high-accuracy and fast-pruned models directly without additional overhead compared to traditional methods, while also reducing the required computational resources by up to 72% and significantly reducing the time required for model pruning by up to 2.3 times more efficiently in terms of both FLOPs and memory usage.

Combining these detections with electromagnetic radiation holds significant potential to improve our comprehension of neutron star events, particularly their dense matter state. However, electromagnetic analysis of gravitational waves necessitates the rapid identification of signals from gravitational waves in real-time. Traditional approaches face substantial challenges in achieving such fast identification due to the computationally intensive nature of gravity wave detection. Furthermore, they are prone to producing false positives. To address these limitations, we propose a novel, machine-learning based detector for neutron star black hole and binary neutron star events. Utilizing the LIGO-Virgo Public Available Data Archive, we collected a comprehensive dataset consisting of signal simulations and noise segments, which we employed to train and test a deep neural network. Our approach demonstrated superior performance in detection accuracy and false alarm rate when compared to traditional methods.

Analysis of this data has shown that the exoplanet, which has an estimated mass roughly equivalent to that of Jupiter, likely formed through migration or by remaining in its original location rather than being formed by a specific high-energy migration mechanism. Two main obstacles arise when attempting to solve CMDPs for the development of optimal operational strategies: they are often characterized by an extremely vast number of states and actions, as well as a difficult-to-compute transition matrix. To resolve these challenges, we develop an algorithm that combines policy iteration with subgradient ascent. We show that this approach allows the CMDP to converge to a solution at a rate proportional to $O(\log(T)/\sqrt{T})$, where T represents the number of iterations, provided that a specific condition is met. This method also offers an efficient way to reduce the dimensionality of the CMDP by exploiting its structural properties when applicable. We successfully apply our algorithm to critical problems with such a structure: multi-product inventory control and multi-class queue management, achieving results superior to existing approaches in terms of computational efficiency.

Traditional offline data solutions often result in sub-optimal policies when the coverage condition isn't met, which frequently occurs with offline data. The pessimism principle resolves this problem by limiting actions with little data usage. Although most pessimism-based methods depend on a key hyperparameter for pessimism, they often don't provide a clear choice or it becomes statistically difficult to set. Our work introduces a novel method that determines pessimism solely from the data without requiring an additional parameter. This model enables us to identify a range of valid dynamic treatment regimes that ensure a certain level of performance for any optimality criterion.

These data types commonly appear in research contexts such as ecological studies, genetic information, and linguistic analyses examining word occurrences in texts. Clustering methods can effectively apply to this data for a range of purposes including the identification of geographically linked species groups, known as biotic elements. Various clustering approaches can be utilized to process such data including the use of latent class mixtures under the assumption of local independence, hierarchical clustering based on the Jaccard distance, or applying European clustering methods to the presence-absence data's corresponding binary Proximity matrix. To address this, this study proposes a novel approach involving the multi-way partition of a matrix that directly takes the presence-absence data structure into consideration. This novel approach is evaluated using the 58 biotic elements in the European flora dataset as selected by the European Vegetation Classification scheme, demonstrating its effectiveness through visual and evaluative assessments as well as from an information perspective.

deep neural networks has received significant attention, but dealing with RGB and RGB-D images separately often necessitates the design of specific network architectures. This paper proposes an efficient and unified structure that integrates cross-attention context extraction to effectively tackle both tasks. By effectively fusing two inputs (for RGB images) or three inputs (for RGB-D images) with a cross-attention mechanism, our framework leverages the rich information present in both RGB and depth features. This structure's simplicity and efficacy enable efficient extraction and fusion of contextual information. As shown by experimental results, our approach outperforms current state-of-the-art methods on various datasets in terms of multiple evaluation metrics.

For subtask A, a BERT-based classifier was adapted and achieved a high macro F1 score of 0.8136 in evaluating test data, thereby ranking 3rd among 103 competitors. Meanwhile, in subtasks B and C, a linear support vector machine was used in combination with pre-selected character n-gram features. Building on this, we developed a method to calculate corrections to the helicity spin jamma relations for spins higher than three through an analysis of the superamplitude's helicity structure. In this context, we defined a correction term that expresses the difference between a helicity spin amplitude and its flat space equivalent, and identified its relationship with a non-compact Aperture representation. Specifically, we expressed the correction term as a sum of terms corresponding to the removal of specific helicity components, and demonstrated that this expression complies with the constraints of supersymmetry. Notably, we observed that the correction term admits a spin-dependent interpretation in terms of mass-deformed $\mathcal{N}$=4 super Yang-Mills theory. Leveraging this picture, we obtained an innovative representation of the two-loop corrections in terms of a mass-dependent variable. Our analysis also reveals a intriguing relationship between the helicity spin amplitude corrections and the superamplitude's maximally helicity violating properties.

, has historically been challenging for object-oriented programming due to inefficiencies in memory allocation and access.  Despite this limitation, a range of applications, including real-world programs with inherent object structures, have been overlooked for parallelization opportunities.  Our research identified a particular subset of object-oriented programming called Single-Method Multiple-Objects (SMMO), which can be efficiently parallelized on SIMD devices by executing the same method across multiple objects of a given type.  To facilitate easy adoption of high-speed GPU programming for average developers, we created the DynaSOAr CUDA framework specifically tailored for SMMO applications.  This framework includes a do-all execution model with adaptive memory allocation, a dynamic data layout optimizer, and a forward data transformation system.  As a result, DynaSOAr enables GPU programming using standard C++11 features, eliminating the need for manual memory management, custom data structures, and low-level GPU APIs.  Our findings from evaluating DynaSOAr on various applications demonstrate up to 80Watt power efficiency and a 70x speedup in GPU programming with DynaSOAr compared to existing solutions, while also showcasing superior memory management and reduced overheads in application scenarios.

, femtosecond X-ray pulse from a free-electron laser causes drastic electronic excitation, triggering swift changes within the material's electronic system that unfold over the duration of the pulse. The amount of X-rays absorbed by the material becomes contingent upon the energy flux, giving rise to a unique form of X-ray absorption near edge spectroscopy. Researchers can study valence excitation on the few-femtosecond timescale with this type of XANES spectroscopy, allowing for in-depth examination of highly excited solids.

To develop a theoretical framework for interpreting high-intensity XANES spectra, researchers combined time-dependent density functional theory with a method for incorporating core excitations, then applied this approach to investigate the absorption spectra of solids subjected to high fluxes of X-rays. Results from density functional theory reveal that the absorption spectra of these materials display an abrupt drop-off at high frequencies at densities approaching the limit of complete ionization.

In a specific examination of molecular nitrogen within a carbon frame, researchers found that the absorption spectra change over the course of a few femtoseconds when the molecule is subjected to high fluxes of X-rays, contrasting with the time-invariant nature of molecular nitrogen's absorption spectra at lower intensity fluxes. The computation also demonstrates that the absorption spectra become contingent upon the molecule's broken bonds when nitrogen atoms are ionized, highlighting the significance of structural features on the edge of absorption spectra at high intensity fluxes.

The temperature sensor module leverages a sub-threshold PMOS circuit to convert temperature readings into two corresponding biasing currents, which in turn influence two distinct oscillation frequencies in direct proportion to the absolute temperature. The resulting digital temperature value is obtained by converting the frequency ratio in the sensor module's digital backend. Research has successfully applied machine learning methods for identifying IoT devices, with positive outcomes; yet current approaches disregard the costs involved in extracting device features from network data. The systems' phases were studied as a function of parameter $d$ and the packing density of molecules $\eta$, under the condition that only repulsive interactions were present. This led to the system's behavior being controlled solely by the entropy of molecular arrangement. For systems where the packing density was below $0.5$, in addition to the standard liquid state, we observed standard nematic and smectic A liquid crystalline phases. Conversely, when the packing density exceeded $0.5$, two distinct non-standard polar crystalline phases emerged alongside the non-polar hexagonal close-packed crystal structure, namely the antiferroelectric splay crystal and the ferroelectric splay crystal. In the parameter $d$ range between $0.78$ and $0.981$, the standard smectic A phase transformed directly into the non-standard polar crystalline phase without going through the standard nematic phase. Moreover, we observed that the length of the longest molecular extension, in relation to the diameter of the smallest sphere, influenced the type of polar crystalline phase that formed, where $d$ acted as a tunable parameter for this effect.

a significant transformation in the field of reversible steganography. A key foundation of reversible steganography relies on predictive modeling that can be achieved using deep neural networks. This has been currently mitigated by limiting data modification bits to only those alterations deemed minimally invasive. In contrast, this study proposes an innovative method where we train a deep learning model to accurately identify and process the data alterations caused by prediction errors, thereby expanding the scope of reversible steganography. In particular, this study presents a novel approach by integrating an attention module into a deep learning model, allowing it to pinpoint and correct distortion bits with an unprecedented level of accuracy. To date, the most successful attention module has been found to outperform other methods in processing data alterations caused by prediction errors. Moreover, this study presents an innovative method for optimizing the depth of the deep learning model, effectively reducing training and deployment complexities. Lastly, this study provides an exhaustive comparison of several optimization methods for selecting the most optimal hyperparameters.

a particular n-tuple $(x_1, \ldots, x_n)$ within the range [0,1] is classified as 'cyclic' when there exist unique, independent random variables $(U_1, \ldots, U_n)$ where the likelihood of $U_{i+1}$ being greater than $U_i$ is $x_i$ for $i$ ranging from 1 to n-1, and the likelihood of $U_1$ being greater than $U_n$ is $x_n$. We represent the likelihood of selecting a random n-tuple that meets these 'cyclic' criteria as $p_n$ and its 'nontransitive' subset as $p_n^*$. However, identifying IBIs from noisy signals is difficult, especially when they are heavily distorted by motion noise, which is common in individuals who are highly active. Researchers working on remote health monitoring and wearable devices have identified signal quality assessment as a crucial step in minimizing error rates. While existing solutions focus on using feature extractors followed by classifiers to predict IBI reliability, they often rely on data that has already been processed and do not effectively utilize raw data for assessment. To address these challenges, a new algorithm has been developed that uses raw data from ECG signals to accurately predict IBIs while operating at high fusion ratios and providing fast results. This novel approach utilizes a customized fusion filter, which includes three unique features such as normalized heart rate, QRS complex detection reliability, and signal frequency characteristics, to assess ECG signal quality. By processing data in real-time, this filter can quickly identify high-quality sections of the ECG signal, which in turn enables reliable IBI detection even in the presence of motion noise. Experimental results demonstrate that this algorithm outperforms existing solutions by achieving an accuracy of 93.46%, a mean absolute error of 32.40 milliseconds, and a standard error of 31.96 milliseconds for 100-sample moving window IBI estimates, as well as a significant reduction in processing time of 80%.

By leveraging experimentally feasible methods of gradual temperature changes, we've developed an approach to create a specific type of heat engine known as an "Olcen." This particular type heat engine is nearly universal and can be implemented using any form of thermal resource that fluctuates over time. 

For instance, an Olcen can be constructed from the thermal vibrations of a magnetized spin, driven by an alternating current. This particular device surpasses the cyclic performance achieved through the well-established principle of minimum waste heat, known as the Curie-Weiss temperature. 

Due to the versatility of the time-varying energy source, it's possible to create an Olcen that operates on thermal cycles that happen extremely slowly, much slower than traditional Olcens that rely on the variation of a magnetic field. This allows for the creation of heat engines that operate on an extremely slow timescale, far slower than the typical timescale of a magnetic relaxation. 

This concept of an Olcen heat engine could potentially be used as an extremely precise tool to study the fine details of a system that operates on a very slow timescale, and it's possible that it requires to be cooled down to temperatures that are very close to absolute zero in order to be useful as a tool to study the behavior of a system that operates on a very slow timescale.

our investigation focuses on how much information a guessing adversary can gain. The underlying source coding problem is represented by a confusion graph, illustrating how source symbols can be distinguished from one another. The adversary's ability to successfully guess the source sequence is measured relative to its prior knowledge, with this measurement maximized over various source distributions. When the adversary follows a specific model where they only make a single guess and can perfectly match their guess to the true sequence, this measurement is known as the maximal leakage in literature and can be expressed as the maximum min-entropy leakage. We establish a comprehensive single-letter representation of the optimal normalized leakage in this adversarial scenario, along with a stochastic coding method that reaches this optimum. Interestingly, our analysis shows that both the optimal leakage and optimal distortion of standard source coding achieve the same maximum value, along with a previously proposed rate distortion function with an added distortion delay of one, all while maintaining the same confusion graph for source and adversary. We further expand our results to cover cases of multiple communicating adversaries.

influence on science by suggesting that he struggled with mathematical proficiency. This perceived weakness drove him to focus on experimentation and empiricism, as well as embracing the telescope's capabilities. His emphasis on hands-on research, which is often credited as an innovative aspect of his scientific approach, might actually be a consequence of his inability to make meaningful mathematical contributions. Similarly, his extensive discussion of basic scientific principles was, arguably, an outcome of his limitations in mathematics, as they often say "those who can't do, teach." It is proposed that Galileo's scientific vision, which is typically viewed as groundbreaking, was actually based on long-established ideas from mathematicians. The main difference lies in that Galileo chose to articulate these ideas in philosophical writing, as his mathematical colleagues preferred to focus on more technical matters. In essence, it is suggested that Galileo's scientific legacy was, in part, a result of his inability to succeed in the highly competitive world of mathematics during the 16th and 17th centuries.
